title.narrative: "Rebuilding Safe and Inclusive Education in Conflict-Affected Rural Aleppo - Learning First"

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThis project addresses the critical shortage of safe, inclusive learning environments in conflict-affected rural Aleppo by comprehensively rehabilitating 5 high-priority public schools in the severely impacted sub-districts of Daret Azza, Atareb, and Tadaf (prioritized per SHF Annex 2b). Directly targeting about 2,300 crisis-affected children and school staff (50% girls), and 3850 Indirect beneficiaries (House Hold) it enables dignified returns and sustainable education access by:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1- Restoring Essential Infrastructure: Rehabilitating 56 classrooms, 10 administrative rooms, constructing 36 gender-segregated accessible WASH facilities and 5 facilities for disability. The proposed project will be repairing 5 playgrounds/schoolyards with safety fencing, and installing solar panels to ensure uninterrupted, multi-shift learning – directly tackling overcrowding and unsafe conditions highlighted in needs assessments.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt2- Building Inclusive Learning Environments: Installing access ramps/rails, distributing 700 school desks and essential educational furniture and learning tools.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt3- Supporting Returnee Integration Retention: Implementing language bridging and remedial classes for 500 returnee children and training 40 teachers in inclusive education and emergency pedagogy to improve learning outcomes and retention.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt4- Strengthening Community Engagement: Launching Back-to-Learning campaigns to enroll about 3000 out-of-school children (OOSC) and establishing Parent-Teacher Associations to foster community ownership and sustainability.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt5- Closely coordinated with the MoE/DoE and Education Sector, the project directly aligns with SHF Envelope1 and 2 priorities by supporting safe returns to communities of origin in high-severity zones (Annex 2b). It tackles key barriers to enrollment, reduces critical overcrowding, and ensures compliance with national standards for protective, inclusive education.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgt6- Following school rehabilitation, this project will enroll approximately 400 children from roughly 10 surrounding villages. It specifically targets communities that were on the military front lines in 2024 and endured widespread destruction, including severe damage to critical infrastructure.lt/pgtltpgt7- According to OCHA's IDP return reports, the number of beneficiaries is expected to rise substantially as most displaced persons return over time.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtFouadi's core mission of delivering integrated child services is powerfully realized through its robust, eight-year strategic partnership with the Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), active since 2017. This highly credible alliance has enabled the implementation of key projects across rural and semi-urban Aleppo Governorate, focusing on education, WASH, and post-earthquake emergency response.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtDemonstrating this impact, Fouadi and SHF have successfully collaborated on:lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1- Essential WASH Support (2017): Providing safe drinking water to 3,080 IDPs (~440 HH) and sanitation facilities to 2,016 IDPs (~288 HH) at Jibreen IDPs Shelter.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt2- Large-Scale Education Infrastructure (2019-2024): The full rehabilitation of 25 schools across four phases, with a total investment of $1,199,705 USD, benefiting approximately 7,000 children and 6,700 households.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt3- Rapid Post-Earthquake Recovery (2023): The emergency rehabilitation of 6 schools, funded by $380,000 USD, restoring education access for ~1,600 children and supporting ~1,950 households.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbrgtFouadi has extensive experience rehabilitating out-of-service schools and also implement education and child protection programs as follows: ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtCurrent UNICEF Projects (2025):lt/pgtltpgtltbrgt1- Teach-Up II ($1.39M): Education for 25,570 children in 6 Aleppo distrs (Al Bab, Dayr Hafir, As-Safira, Jebel Saman, Al-Khafsa, Maskana).ltbrgt2- Nour II ($1.64M): Child protection (safe spaces PSS) for 125,400 children in same 6 Aleppo distrs.ltbrgt3- Basic Needs Support ($710K): Cash transfers to impoverished families w/ children in Aleppo/Idleb slums.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThis demonstrates we are an ideal partner for the proposed project activities.ltbrgtlt/pgt
